programme: HDAC3-mediated histone deacetylation setting the transcriptional tone of stress- and injury-responsive glial/neuronal genes, with ETV5 acting on the same inflammatory-restraint side of the circuit in stroke (via HACE1/Nrf2 suppression of microglial M1 polarization)
role_in_a: In IBS, HDAC3-dependent histone acetylation changes in the amygdala are reported to sensitize visceral pain circuitry after early-life stress, i.e. HDAC3 sits in the brain-gut stress-sensitization arm of IBS rather than in gut epithelium directly.
role_in_b: In stroke, HDAC3 activity in microglia/vasculature shapes the acute post-ischemic inflammatory response, and pharmacologic HDAC modulation (e.g. valproic acid) is neuroprotective; ETV5 independently restrains microglial M1 polarization through HACE1/Nrf2 signalling after ischemia, placing both factors on the injury-limiting side of stroke neuroinflammation.
shared_axis: Both diseases have a stress/inflammation-sensitized neuroglial component — IBS through central stress circuitry, stroke through peri-infarct microglia — and HDAC3 is the epigenetic control point reported in each independently; if that control point is shared mechanistically rather than coincidentally, it would predict that manipulating HDAC3 changes both visceral pain sensitization and post-stroke glial inflammatory tone.
reasoning: HDAC3 clears the bar for 'supported' because each disease has its own direct paper (stress/visceral hypersensitivity for IBS, microglial neuroinflammation and HDAC-pathway neuroprotection for stroke), but no retrieved paper connects the two diseases through it, and IBS's own Open Targets percentile for HDAC3 is very low (0.07), which sits awkwardly next to a paper claiming a CNS mechanistic role. Only ETV5 adds a second data point, and only on the stroke side, so the account leans heavily on two factors rather than a broadly corroborated module; the other nine concordant factors either returned nothing or returned literature that, on inspection, does not actually support them (see caveats).
support: 35600618 — HDAC3/histone acetylation in the amygdala drives early-life-stress visceral hypersensitivity (IBS). 42677156 — pH-responsive HDAC-targeted nanoparticle delivery dampens microglia-mediated neuroinflammation (stroke). 42517197 — melatonin plus valproic acid (HDAC pathway) is protective in cerebral ischemia (stroke). 40562126 — ETV5 improves ischemic stroke outcome by suppressing microglial M1 polarization via the HACE1/Nrf2 axis (stroke).
how_to_falsify: In the same lab, inhibit or knock down HDAC3 selectively in stress-circuit/amygdalar neurons in an IBS visceral-hypersensitivity model and in microglia in a matched cerebral-ischemia model; if HDAC3 loss fails to blunt both the visceral pain phenotype and the infarct-associated microglial inflammatory response, the proposed shared epigenetic switch does not hold. Separately, test whether ETV5 modulation has any measurable effect on gut/enteric immune signalling relevant to IBS (its target list includes IFNG, IL10, IL17A/F, CXCL cytokines) — if it has none, its inclusion in the story is unwarranted.
caveats: The network's expression tissues are blood (stroke) and colorectal (IBS), but the only literature support that is genuinely on-topic is central-nervous-system (amygdala, microglia) — a mismatch between where the network was built and where the mechanism is documented. Only 12 patient-group comparisons were available from 2 independent cohort pairs, a narrow base for the recurrence fractions, including HDAC3's 9/12. The retrieved 'support' for MSC (41480397, 42351306) and DLX3 (41555399) is very likely a name/topic collision — mesenchymal-stem-cell therapy papers matching the MSC gene symbol, and bone/osteogenesis papers matching the DLX-family homeobox factors — not evidence about these transcription factors' roles in IBS or stroke, so both were excluded from the account despite appearing well-supported at first read. MAZ's single stroke-adjacent paper (29209328) concerns a coronary-artery-disease serum antibody marker, not cerebrovascular pathology, so it was not used either. Tissue-generic exclusions (FOXO3, FLI1, TCF4, DNMT1, EPAS1, GLI1, HLX, ETS1, LEF1, KLF2, E2F3, FOXO1) removed several plausible immune/vascular regulators before ranking, so their absence reflects the filter, not a finding that they are uninvolved; single-view factors (ATOH7, IRX4, SATB1, HMGA1, MYF6, HSF1, OVOL1, MYOCD, NCOA4, ZXDC) were correctly excluded as one-group artefacts.
